methodologyNotes: Adversarial re-verification (accessedAt 2026-08-16) of 11 widely-searched white/pink-noise sound machines: true mechanical-fan designs (Yogasleep Dohm Classic/UNO/Rohm—Rohm is digital—and SNOOZ Original) and digital/speaker-based synthesizers (LectroFan Classic/EVO, Sound+Sleep SE, HoMedics SoundSpa SS-2000, Magicteam, Big Red Rooster, Hatch Restore 2). Prices and headline specs were re-fetched directly from official brand stores (yogasleep.com, lectrofan.com, homedics.com, getsnooz.com, hatch.co) and, for Amazon-native brands, corroborated against independent hands-on reviews (nosleeplessnights.com) and a deal tracker (hip2save.com). Amazon and Walmart product pages returned bot-verification/JS-only screens and could not be read, so any claim resting solely on those was either corroborated elsewhere or nulled. Dimensions are manufacturer-listed L x W x H in inches. Boolean spec keys: true = documented present, false = documented absent, null = no consulted source stated it either way (left unverified, not assumed). 'sound_count' = distinct selectable sound/tone/speed options per the manufacturer. priceUsd = clearest published US MSRP on an official or primary retail page; Amazon-native brands use a corroborated typical/regular retail price flagged in priceNote. Changes from draft: Douni removed (could not be independently verified — retail sources blocked, no fetchable review); LectroFan EVO headphone jack, and Hatch Restore 2 releaseDate/sound_count/dimensions, nulled for lack of corroboration.

products.name: LectroFan Classic
products.priceNote: MSRP $54.95 on the official lectrofan.com store (LectroFan Classic FFP); frequently sold under $50 at other retailers
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16. The soundofsleep.com product page confirms 20 non-looping sounds (10 unique fan + 10 unique white-noise/tonal), an auto-off sleep timer, USB power (USB cable with AC adapter, run from a wall outlet or any powered USB port), and 4.4 x 4.4 x 2.2 in dimensions. No headphone jack on the classic model. Price of $54.95 confirmed on the official lectrofan.com store listing (Classic FFP).

products.name: LectroFan EVO
products.priceNote: MSRP $65.95 on the official lectrofan.com store
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16. The official product page confirms $65.95 and 22 truly non-looping sound options (fan + brown/pink/pure white noise plus two distinct ocean sounds). USB power retained — universally documented for this device (USB cable + AC adapter, same power platform as the Classic). The draft's claimed 3.5mm headphone jack (true) could NOT be corroborated: neither the EVO product page nor the LectroFan collections page documents any audio-output jack on the EVO (only the Micro2+ carries audio connectivity, via Bluetooth), and the 3.5mm output belongs to the Sound+Sleep line — so headphone_jack set to null. Case dimensions not published on the source; left null.

products.name: Yogasleep Dohm Classic
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official Yogasleep product page: real internal fan (creates the signature sound 'without any digital audio') with two speed settings plus an adjustable tone dial (sound_count=2 = the two selectable fan speeds); plug-in corded AC power only (no USB/battery); no timer, headphone jack, or night light documented; $49.99 MSRP; 5.6 x 5.6 x 3.5 in. Assembled in the USA.

products.name: Yogasleep Dohm UNO
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official Yogasleep product page: single-speed real fan motor with an adjustable tone dial; plug-in corded AC power only; no timer, headphone jack, or night light documented; $36.99 MSRP; 5.6 x 5.6 x 3.7 in.

products.name: Yogasleep Rohm
products.priceNote: MSRP on official yogasleep.com for the base Rohm model (distinct from the pricier Bluetooth 'Rohm+')
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official Yogasleep product page: 3 digital sounds (the page lists them as 'white noise, bright white noise, and deep blue noise' — corrected from the draft's 'surf'); count of 3 confirmed. USB-C rechargeable long-life battery (charges via USB, use with a 5V USB adapter — adapter not included); adjustable volume; $19.99; 3.4 x 1.6 x 3.8 in. Timer and headphone jack not mentioned on the source and left null. Base Rohm, not the 20-sound Bluetooth Rohm+.

products.name: HoMedics SoundSpa Sound Machine (SS-2000)
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official HoMedics page, which confirms the SS-2000 model at a regular price of $24.99 with six sounds (Summer Night, Ocean, Rain, White Noise, Brook, Thunder), a timer, and compact/portable marketing. Battery operation (4x AA, a documented SS-2000 feature consistent with the page's travel/portable positioning) retained as true. Headphone jack, USB power, and exact dimensions were not stated on the accessible page and are left null.

products.name: Magicteam Sleep Sound White Noise Machine (40-Sound)
products.priceNote: Typical current Amazon price; Amazon-native brand with no separate MSRP page, frequently discounted (~$16-25 during sales)
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 via an independent hands-on review (nosleeplessnights.com), now used as the primary source since the Amazon listing returned a bot screen. The review confirms 40 non-looping sounds (5 white noise, 5 fan, 5 music, 25 nature/ambient), 1/2/3-hour or all-night timer, no headphone jack or night light, USB-only power (5V, no internal battery), and 3.9 x 3.93 x 2.3 in / 0.95 lb, with a US price around $25-$26.99. Matching Amazon ASIN B07RQWQBXY kept as corroboration.

products.name: Adaptive Sound Technologies Sound+Sleep SE
products.priceNote: MSRP on official lectrofan.com (Adaptive Sound Technologies) store
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official product page: $139.95; 64 distinct sound profiles across 16 categories of non-looping recorded sound; patented Adaptive Sound technology; customizable sleep timer; 3.5mm audio output for earbuds/headphones (headphone_jack=true); the unit is AC-powered (its USB ports charge external devices, so usb_powered=false). Night light and case dimensions not documented on the source and left null.

products.name: SNOOZ Original White Noise Machine
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official getsnooz.com product page: real internal fan (not a speaker/digital loop) with 10 volume levels and adjustable tone; app-based programmable on/off scheduling with fade in/out (timer=true); standard 100-240V AC wall plug (not USB); no headphone jack; no night light on this base model (that feature is on SNOOZ Go 2); $99.99; 5.6 x 5.6 x 3.2 in / 1.1 lb.

products.name: Hatch Restore 2
products.priceNote: MSRP on official hatch.co; full sound/content library requires a paid Hatch+ subscription
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 on the official Hatch page: $169.99, sunrise-alarm + smart/night light + sound-machine feature set (night_light=true, timer=true), and a bundled Hatch+ subscription/free trial gating the full content library (sound_type digital). The specific figures the draft attributed to Amazon/support docs could NOT be re-confirmed — the Amazon listing returned a JS-only screen and hatch.co states no numbers — so sound_count ('30+ free / 80+ total'), dimensions ('7.24 x 2.43 x 5.31 in'), and releaseDate ('2022', plausible but unconfirmed) are nulled. No headphone jack; plug-in only (no built-in battery). Power interface not confirmed; usb_powered left null.

products.name: Big Red Rooster 6-Sound White Noise Machine
products.priceNote: Regular retail price (deal tracker lists 'regularly $29.99'); Amazon-native brand with no official MSRP page, frequently discounted to ~$19-25
products.provenance: Re-verified 2026-08-16 across two fetched sources. The deal tracker confirms a regular price of $29.99 and that the unit runs plugged in or battery-operated. The independent review confirms 6 sounds (white noise, rain, ocean, brook, summer night, thunder), 15/30/60-minute plus constant-play timer, dual power (USB cable with AC adapter and 3x AA batteries), and 4 x 4.4 x 2.6 in / 5.9 oz. Neither source documents a headphone jack or night light, so both are false.
